lines.speaker: Snow
lines.english: Hey Karen, aren’t you going to Malaysia soon ?

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.english: Yes! I’m so nervous right now about going to Malaysia.

lines.speaker: Snow
lines.english: Is there...some new development in your career?

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.english: Uh...there is. Hmm... you could say I’m being invited to...

lines.speaker: Snow
lines.english: I see!

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.english: ...to represent Hong Kong artists in an exchange there and...I’ll be teaching them batik. But it’s kind of weird, since batik actually comes from over there, around Malaysia. Anyway someone there knows me and is willing to sponsor my...fees. So...yes. I’ll be going there as a Hong Kong artist. That’s why I’m so excited for it.

lines.speaker: Snow
lines.english: That sounds great. How long will you be there?

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.english: For three months.

lines.speaker: Snow
lines.english: Wow! Three months? That’s quite a long time. Is your family...okay with that?

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.english: Um...tsk...uh...about that. Haha, you know. Hong Kong...I mean Chinese...families traditionally think...like they don’t think girls should...uh...be so career-minded.

lines.speaker: Snow
lines.english: Yeah...

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.english: They’d rather their daughters settle with a good pier (husband)...and so on.

lines.speaker: Snow
lines.english: I see...

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.english: I mean you know...uh...nah I suppose you already understand.

lines.speaker: Snow
lines.english: Yes I do, I understand. But...to be honest, going there for three months sounds pretty dangerous, so I think your family are bound to be worried...but anyway if you...like if you weren’t going for three months but instead staying in Hong Kong and working as an artist anyway...in that case...

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.english: But not many...I wouldn’t have many opportunities.

lines.speaker: Snow
lines.english: Really?

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.english: I mean it’s...quite funny actually. Let’s say maybe...tsk, for one you still face keen competition once you’re in the ‘outside world’, but...but sometimes, by arriving at a place as a foreigner, like...you might get more favourable opportunities. In contrast...if I’m in Hong Kong holding these activities, I might not garner that much attention (influence). And...it all depends on the odds, right? I mean...when I get an opportunity, I seize it.

lines.speaker: Snow
lines.english: It’s true. I understand how small Hong Kong’s artistic market is, since I work in photography myself, which is...quite challenging and strenuous. Besides...especially tsk, not only is it hard to establish a career, I feel like the pressure from family is even worse. Like...my family members...to be honest, none of my family members support me.

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.english: Right.

lines.speaker: Snow
lines.english: I wonder if you’re going through similar troubles too.

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.english: For sure I am, especially from my mom.

lines.speaker: Snow
lines.english: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.english: I don’t even know why but moms tend to be more...unwilling for their children to go through hardship.

lines.speaker: Snow
lines.english: Ah yes yes yes.

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.english: But...my dad is better (more positive) now. Me and my dad took...almost half a year...or even a year. I don’t even know, maybe an entire year, maybe half a year really...to communicate, as in I actually brought it up and discussed it with him. Right now, half a year later, he’s finally accepted the fact that I’m going to Malaysia. So he hasn’t...he’s stopped objecting and started uh...checking on me so I’m starting to feel that my daddy has accepted my plans.

lines.speaker: Snow
lines.english: Right.

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.english: Whereas mom is...alright. What about you?

lines.speaker: Snow
lines.english: Well...in my case, my mom doesn’t...prefer me working on...because doing photography requires me to go all over the place, which my mom doesn’t a fan of.

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.english: It’s pretty gruelling too, having to carry all that...equipment around.

lines.speaker: Snow
lines.english: Yes, yes. But I’ve...well initially, back when I started, I would carry a backpack because...uh the equipment can get quite heavy. Later on I bought a suitcase, which is better, but my mom is like, uh isn’t your suitcase heavy? She would rather I worked as like uh...an OL (office lady), that kind of job, because, you know, I’ve received higher education and she’d rather I didn’t have to run around.

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.english: Hmm...
